gloss: to see; to come across; to catch sight of

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {目|め}にしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to see; to come across; to catch sight of
definitions.explanation: To happen to see something or someone, often implying an unplanned or incidental encounter rather than deliberate looking.

examples.japanese: ⟦{珍|めずら}しい→珍しい：01200_mezurashii⟧⟦{光景|こうけい}→光景：02799_koukei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{目|め}にした。
examples.english: I came across a rare sight.

examples.japanese: ⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦ニュース→ニュース：04437_nyuusu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{目|め}にして⟦{驚|おどろ}いた→驚く：01255_odoroku⟧。
examples.english: I was surprised when I saw that news.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{偶然|ぐうぜん}→偶然：02674_guuzen⟧⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{友人|ゆうじん}→友人：03649_yuujin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{目|め}にして、⟦{思|おも}わ→思う：00492_omou⟧ず⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけた→かける：00854_kakeru⟧。
examples.english: I happened to spot an old friend in front of the station and called out to them without thinking.

notes:
An idiomatic expression meaning to see or catch sight of something, often implying that the encounter was unplanned or incidental. It carries a slightly more literary or formal tone than ⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧.

USAGE:
- Often used when encountering something unexpectedly or for the first time
- Common in written Japanese and news reporting
- Frequently appears in the past tense ({目|め}にした)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{光景|こうけい}→光景：02799_koukei⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{目|め}にする: to witness a scene
- ⟦{記事|きじ}→記事：00227_kiji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{目|め}にする: to come across an article
- ⟦{現実|げんじつ}→現実：02720_genjitsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{目|め}にする: to see the reality
- ⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧{目|め}にする: to see for the first time

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧: the basic word for seeing; neutral and general
- ⟦{見|み}かける→見かける：01644_mikakeru⟧: to happen to see someone; implies spotting a person
- ⟦{目撃|もくげき}する→目撃する：20232_mokugekisuru⟧: to witness (more dramatic, often used for accidents or crimes)
